name: Colored-Ideal Parametrization of the Dismantlable-Ample Basis
statement: Up to partial-cube isomorphism, the complete pc-minimal obstruction basis for dismantlable ampleness is the disjoint union of the antipodally punctured cubes $Q_n^{--}$, $n\ge3$, and the hyperoctahedral orbits of full-transversal ideals $J\in\mathfrak B_d^{\mathrm{col}}$: $J$ has a $d$-linear resolution but no linear-quotient order, uses both literals of every color, and all two restriction images and the contraction image in every color have linear quotients. Equivalently, an irredundant ample $X\subseteq Q_d$ is a forbidden pc-minor exactly when $X\notin\mathsf{Damp}$ but all $3d$ elementary pc-minors belong to $\mathsf{Damp}$. Within the ample layer, cornerless obstructions are exactly those whose ideal loses $d$-linearity after deleting any minimal generator.
proof: A full-transversal ideal recovers an irredundant cube family. Its linear resolution is equivalent to ampleness and failure of linear quotients to failure of dismantlability. The three one-color maps are exactly the ideals of the two elementary restrictions and the elementary contraction. If these images have linear quotients, all elementary pc-minors are dismantlable; pc-minor closure then handles every proper minor. Conversely every ample pc-minimal obstruction satisfies these four ideal conditions. Uniqueness of an irredundant cube embedding gives the quotient by coordinate permutations and reorientations. The nonample-layer theorem supplies precisely the punctured cubes. Finally, deleting a concept preserves ampleness exactly when deleting its ideal generator preserves $d$-linearity, proving the corner criterion.
